title: Does zeolite (clinoptilolite) actually bind and remove heavy metals?

grade.title: At least one good randomized trial, or consistent human evidence from more than one source
grade.outcome: Blocking uptake of lead swallowed at the same time
grade.basis: One double-blind randomized tracer study (n=42). Three authors were employed by the sponsor. Not evidence about stored metal.

answerHtml: In a randomized tracer study, healthy adults who took purified clinoptilolite with a lead isotope absorbed less of that dose than the placebo group. Maximum 204Pb enrichment was 0.505 percent with placebo versus 0.073 percent and 0.057 percent with the two active arms. The corpus describes this as about 90 percent lower enteral uptake. The study does not show removal of lead already stored in the body.

sections.heading: Study
sections.html: Samekova and colleagues (2021) enrolled 42 healthy adults. The outcome was enteral uptake of a 204Pb tracer and urinary tracer, not a clinical endpoint. doi:10.1038/s41598-021-94245-x. PMID 34285282.
